name: The Orkney Islands
tagline: A remote archipelago holding one of the world's densest concentrations of Neolithic monuments, older than Stonehenge and the pyramids alike.
highlight: Standing inside Skara Brae's stone houses, genuinely more complete and intact than most homes I've seen from centuries far more recent.
shortDescription: A remote northern archipelago home to Skara Brae, the Ring of Brodgar and some of the best-preserved Neolithic sites anywhere in the world.
metaDescription: An Orkney Islands travel guide: Skara Brae, the Ring of Brodgar, Maeshowe, food and how to plan a visit to Scotland's ancient northern isles.

intro: Orkney is genuinely one of the most archaeologically significant places on Earth, a remote northern archipelago holding one of the world's densest concentrations of Neolithic monuments, many still remarkably intact.

Skara Brae, its most famous site, is genuinely older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids, a Stone Age village so well preserved that its stone furniture still stands in place after being buried in sand for thousands of years.

Most visitors genuinely base themselves in Kirkwall, Orkney's small capital, using it to explore a UNESCO World Heritage core of ancient sites within a short drive, alongside more recent history at the poignant Italian Chapel.

whyVisit.intro: Orkney's case rests on genuinely being one of the most important prehistoric landscapes anywhere in the world.

points.title: Skara Brae is genuinely older than Stonehenge
points.text: A remarkably intact Neolithic village, its stone furniture still standing after 5,000 years.

points.title: The Ring of Brodgar is genuinely one of Britain's great stone circles
points.text: A vast Neolithic monument on a narrow strip of land between two lochs.

points.title: Maeshowe is genuinely a masterpiece of ancient engineering
points.text: A chambered cairn precisely aligned to the winter solstice sunset.

points.title: The Italian Chapel is genuinely a moving piece of more recent history
points.text: Built by WWII prisoners of war from a Nissen hut and scrap materials.

points.title: It rewards genuinely visitors willing to travel further north
points.text: A real sense of remoteness and discovery, even for well-travelled visitors.

attractionsIntro: Orkney's essential sights combine genuinely world-significant Neolithic monuments with more recent, moving history.

attractions.name: Skara Brae

image.alt: The Neolithic village of Skara Brae on Orkney

attractions.text: Genuinely older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids, a Stone Age village remarkably preserved after millennia buried in sand.
attractions.tip: The genuinely visitor centre's replica house lets you handle reconstructions of what the original furniture would have felt like.

attractions.name: The Ring of Brodgar

image.alt: The Ring of Brodgar stone circle on Orkney

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Britain's largest stone circles, a vast Neolithic monument set dramatically between two lochs.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free and unstaffed — visit at sunrise or sunset for a genuinely striking atmosphere.

attractions.name: St Magnus Cathedral, Kirkwall

image.file: File:Orkney Islands - Kirkwall, St Magnus Cathedral, Graveyard - 20210816163833.jpg
image.alt: St Magnus Cathedral in Kirkwall, Orkney

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking red sandstone cathedral founded in 1137, still the proud centrepiece of Kirkwall's compact old town.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free to enter, with real medieval atmosphere inside its red and yellow sandstone nave.

attractions.name: The Standing Stones of Stenness

image.alt: The Standing Stones of Stenness on Orkney

attractions.text: Genuinely among the oldest henge monuments in the British Isles, towering stones that predate the nearby Ring of Brodgar.
attractions.tip: Genuinely combine with the Ring of Brodgar, since both sit only a short walk or drive apart.

attractions.name: Maeshowe

image.alt: The Maeshowe chambered cairn on Orkney

attractions.text: Genuinely a masterpiece of Neolithic engineering, a chambered tomb precisely aligned so the winter solstice sunset lights its inner chamber.
attractions.tip: Book genuinely a guided tour ahead — entry to the chamber itself is guide-led only.

attractions.name: The Italian Chapel
attractions.text: Genuinely a deeply moving piece of more recent history, an ornate chapel built by WWII Italian prisoners of war from two Nissen huts.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the interior's painted details, made from scrap materials, reward a slow, close look.

attractions.name: Kirkwall

image.alt: The town of Kirkwall on Orkney

attractions.text: Genuinely Orkney's small, historic capital, its narrow flagstone streets anchored by St Magnus Cathedral.
attractions.tip: Genuinely well set up as a base, with the widest choice of accommodation and restaurants on the islands.

thingsToDoIntro: Orkney genuinely rewards a slow, unhurried pace, moving between ancient sites within a genuinely compact UNESCO World Heritage core.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Skara Brae's ancient village

image.alt: Walking through the ancient village of Skara Brae

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely absorbing hour or two, walking among Stone Age houses complete with original stone beds and dressers.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with nearby Skaill House, a 17th-century mansion included with entry.

thingsToDo.title: Walk among the Ring of Brodgar's stones

image.file: File:Stenness Ring of Brodgar seen closeby 1.jpg
image.alt: Walking among the stones of the Ring of Brodgar

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quiet, atmospheric walk around one of Britain's great stone circles, free and open at any hour.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely visit at sunrise or sunset for the most striking light and atmosphere.

thingsToDo.title: Enter Maeshowe's ancient chamber

image.alt: The entrance passage to Maeshowe's ancient chamber

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rare chance to crawl through a low entrance passage into a still-intact 5,000-year-old burial chamber.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book well ahead, especially around the December solstice when demand peaks.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Italian Chapel

image.alt: Visiting the Italian Chapel on Orkney

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely moving half-hour, taking in the ornate interior painted by homesick prisoners of war from salvaged materials.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely free to enter, though donations toward its upkeep are welcomed.

thingsToDo.title: Explore St Magnus Cathedral

image.file: File:Orkney Islands - Kirkwall, St Magnus Cathedral, Graveyard - 20200816163003.jpg
image.alt: Exploring the interior of St Magnus Cathedral

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely peaceful stop in Kirkwall, exploring nearly 900 years of continuous religious history.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely free to enter, with occasional guided tower tours available in season.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Kirkwall's harbour

image.alt: The harbour at Kirkwall on Orkney

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to end a day of ancient sites, watching the boats along Kirkwall's working harbour.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a good spot to find dinner after a full day exploring the islands.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make an Orkney visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely Maeshowe's guided tour well ahead — entry is guide-led only and slots are limited.
Pack genuinely proper windproof and waterproof layers regardless of season.
Check genuinely ferry schedules closely if bringing a car, especially outside summer.
Allow genuinely a full day for the Skara Brae, Ring of Brodgar and Stenness core sites.
Bring genuinely cash as a backup for smaller rural sites and shops.
Budget genuinely extra time for weather delays — Orkney's exposed position means real disruption is possible.

faq.q: How many days do you need on Orkney?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers the main Neolithic sites, Kirkwall and the Italian Chapel comfortably.

faq.q: Is Skara Brae older than Stonehenge?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — Skara Brae dates back around 5,000 years, predating both Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.

faq.q: Can you visit Orkney as a day trip?
faq.a: It's genuinely possible by flight from Inverness or Edinburgh, but rushed — the islands reward at least an overnight stay.
Genuinely one of the world's densest concentrations of well-preserved Neolithic monuments, alongside striking Northern Isles scenery.

faq.q: Do you need to book Maeshowe in advance?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely essential — entry to the inner chamber is by guided tour only, and slots fill up, especially around the winter solstice.

faq.q: Is Orkney part of the Scottish Highlands?
faq.a: No, genuinely a distinct island group known as the Northern Isles, with its own separate Norse-influenced history and culture.
